name: YeePDF – PDF Builder for Fluent Forms
author: add-ons.org

sections.description:
YeePDF – PDF Builder for Fluent Forms turns every Fluent Forms submission into a PDF document built from your own drag-and-drop template: certificates, quotes, contracts, invoices, tickets, reports, application copies and more — no coding required.

The plugin plugs straight into the Fluent Forms Integrations system. Add a PDF Template Feed to a form, pick a template, and every submission generates a PDF that is attached to the form’s email notifications. Works with the free version of Fluent Forms – Fluent Forms Pro is not required.

Fluent Forms is a trademark of WPManageNinja LLC. This plugin is an independent add-on developed by add-ons.org and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by WPManageNinja.

DEMO: https://pdf.add-ons.org/
DOCUMENTS: https://pdf.add-ons.org/fluentforms-pdf/
Download Pro Version: https://add-ons.org/plugin/pdf-for-fluentforms/

Why Choose YeePDF for Fluent Forms?

  • Native Fluent Forms integration feed — no extra settings page
  • Works with Fluent Forms free and Fluent Forms Pro
  • Drag-and-drop PDF builder with live preview
  • Every Fluent Forms smart code works inside the template
  • PDFs attached to email notifications automatically
  • As many PDF feeds per form as you need, each with its own template
  • Custom file name and password protection per feed
  • Multilingual and RTL ready, custom fonts
  • Generated on your own server — no third-party service

Key Features

Drag and Drop PDF Builder

Design PDF templates with rows, columns, text, images, image lists, text lists, titles, buttons, dividers and spacers. Each block has its own padding, background, alignment, font and border settings. Preview the result instantly while editing.

Fluent Forms Smart Codes

Pick a form in the template editor and insert any field with one click. All Fluent Forms smart codes are supported: {inputs.email}, {inputs.names.first_name}, {all_data}, {submission.id}, {submission.serial_number}, {submission.created_at}, {user.display_name}, {wp.site_title}… plus {form_title}, {form_id} and {entry_id}.

Email PDF Attachments

The generated PDF is attached to every email notification of the form — to the admin, to the submitter, or both. Add several feeds to the same form to generate several PDFs per submission.

File Name and Password

Name each PDF with smart codes (e.g. invoice-{submission.id}) and optionally encrypt it with a password, also built from smart codes.

Paper Size, Orientation, Fonts

Use A4/Letter or custom paper sizes, portrait or landscape, set the margins and upload your own fonts.

Multilingual Support

Generate PDFs in any language, including RTL languages, with DejaVu fonts bundled.

Privacy and Security

PDFs are rendered directly on your server; nothing is sent to an external service.

Popular Use Cases

  • Certificates – personalised certificates after a course or event registration.
  • Quotes & Estimates – professional quotations sent straight to the customer.
  • Contracts & Agreements – contracts filled with the submitted data and attached to the email.
  • Event Tickets – downloadable tickets with the attendee details.
  • Reports & Summaries – structured PDF reports of every submission.
  • Application Forms – printable copies of applications and registrations.

Upgrade to Pro

The Pro add-on is a separate plugin sold on add-ons.org. It adds:

  • Choose Email Notifications – decide which notifications receive each PDF.
  • Advanced table block – styled tables for lists and reports.
  • QR codes, barcodes and signature blocks – generated from form data.
  • Page breaks and 4–7 column layouts.
  • Watermarks – custom text or image watermarks.
  • Headers and footers – branding, page numbers and document metadata on every page.
  • Dropbox integration – save a copy of every generated PDF to Dropbox.
  • Conditional logic – show or hide blocks depending on the submitted values.
  • Priority support – one year of dedicated technical support and updates.

Third-party services

This plugin works entirely on your own server: templates are rendered with the bundled mPDF library and the generated files are stored in your WordPress uploads folder. It does not connect to any external service and does not collect or send any data. Links to pdf.add-ons.org and add-ons.org are documentation and support links only.

(The optional Dropbox upload is part of the separate Pro add-on, which documents it on its own.)

How to Use

Step 1 — Create a PDF template (skip this to use the default template)

  1. Go to PDF Templates in your WordPress admin menu.
  2. Click New Template and design your PDF with the drag-and-drop builder.
  3. Pick your form in the Fluent Forms dropdown at the top of the editor to list its fields, then insert them as smart codes.
  4. Publish the template.

Step 2 — Connect the template to your form

  1. Edit your form in Fluent Forms and open Settings & Integrations > Integrations.
  2. Click Add New Integration and choose PDF Template Feed.
  3. Fill in the feed and click Save Feed:
    • Name – a label for this feed.
    • PDF Template – the template to generate (required).
    • File Name – file name without extension; leave empty to auto-generate. Smart codes allowed, e.g. invoice-{submission.id}.
    • Password Protection – encrypt the PDF with this password; leave empty for none. Smart codes allowed.
    • Status – enable or disable the feed.

From now on every submission of the form generates the PDF and attaches it to the form’s email notifications. Add another feed for a second PDF. To stop, disable or delete the feed.
sections.installation:
1. Download yeepdf-for-fluentforms.zip.
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, choose the zip and click Install Now.
  3. Activate the plugin. A sample template Fluent Forms Default is created under PDF Templates.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require Fluent Forms?

Yes. It extends Fluent Forms and requires it to be installed and activated. The free version of Fluent Forms is enough; Fluent Forms Pro is only needed for the feed’s own conditional logic (a Fluent Forms Pro feature).

Where are the PDF settings for my form?

Edit the form, open Settings & Integrations > Integrations, click Add New Integration and choose PDF Template Feed.

Which smart codes can I use in the template?

Any Fluent Forms smart code: {inputs.field_name} for fields ({inputs.names.first_name} for sub fields), {all_data} for the full submission table, {submission.id}, {submission.serial_number}, {submission.created_at}, {user.*}, {wp.*}. The plugin also adds {form_title}, {form_id} and {entry_id}. Select the form in the template editor to see the list of its fields.

Is the PDF attached to every email notification?

Yes, the PDF is attached to all email notifications of the form. The separate Pro add-on lets you pick which notifications get each PDF.

Can I generate more than one PDF per submission?

Yes. Add as many PDF feeds as you need to the same form, each with its own template, file name and password.

Where are the generated files stored?

In your WordPress uploads folder. The URL of the last PDF is also saved on the submission (_yeepdf_pdf_<feed id> submission meta) for developers.

Can I change the data before the PDF is rendered?

Yes. Use the yeepdf_fluentforms_entry_datas filter to add or change values, and yeepdf_fluentforms_generated_pdf to act on the generated file.
